questions.q: Where is the Semantic Model Builder available?
options: Only inside the Salesforce mobile app
In Tableau Next and in Data 360
Only in Apex classes
Only in Tableau Desktop
questions.explain: The builder is available in Tableau Next and in Data 360 (formerly Data Cloud), where a Semantic Layer area lists models and metrics.

questions.q: Which of these can be used as data objects in a semantic model, according to current documentation?
options: Only CSV files on a laptop
Only Apex triggers
Only page layouts
Data model objects, data lake objects, or calculated insights
questions.explain: Semantic models combine DMOs, DLOs, and calculated insights, so earlier Data 360 work can be reused.

questions.q: What is the right stance toward a formula drafted by Draft with Einstein in a calculated field?
options: Accept it without review because AI is always right
Treat it as a starting point and review it before relying on it
Delete it, since AI cannot draft formulas
Publish it directly to all users
questions.explain: AI-drafted logic can be wrong or misaligned with the business definition, so it must be reviewed and tested.

questions.q: In the suggested modeling workflow, what is the purpose of the final step?
options: To rename the workspace
To delete unused metrics
To hide the model from consumers
To test the model against numbers you already trust, such as a native report, before sharing it
questions.explain: Reconciling the model against a known-good source catches wrong joins and definitions before others rely on it.

questions.q: Which is an accurate statement about consumers of a semantic model?
options: Only Tableau Next dashboards can use it; no other tool can
Only Apex code can read it
Tableau Next, metrics, AI-assisted analytics, and Tableau Desktop or Cloud through the Semantics connector can consume the same model
It can only be read by its creator
questions.explain: One semantic model can serve several consumers, which is the main reason to invest in modeling once.
